cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama State Senate District 14 in 2026. She advanced from a canceled Democratic primary and lost the general election to incumbent Republican April Weaver. Her work history and offices held could not be verified from the sources collected.

endorsements.text: Listed on the voter guide 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' (a Sway voting group by Vote for Peace), as reported by Ballotpedia.
Listed on the voter guide 'Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust' (a Sway voting group by Tabitha Isner), as reported by Ballotpedia.
Listed on the voter guide 'The Neighborhood Guy's Candidates Jamboree' (a Sway voting group by Keith Williams), as reported by Ballotpedia.
Listed on the voter guide 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' (a Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis), as reported by Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Mandie Ledkins was born or raised, or when she came to Alabama. We couldn't find her occupation, work history or any previous elected office. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and we found no campaign-site statements, interviews or questionnaires, so we have no documented positions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, education or policing. We found no news coverage of controversies and no information on foreign ties.

cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 14 since July 2021. Served in the Alabama House (District 49) 2010–2020. Nurse and business executive; former regional director at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, and hospital operations and government-relations director.
cands.gaps: We could not find where April Weaver was born or raised, or when she came to Alabama. We found no documented actions or stated positions of hers on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or education. The list of bills she sponsored did not load on the page we read. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2021, 2022 or 2026, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for her 2026 race. We found no controversies, foreign ties or public statements on data centers or development.
